title: AI Maestro Project Plan
description: Canonical schema for board/plan.json — the project plan every epic and ticket is scoped against. Items carry stable ids (D-/UC-/FR-/NFR-/M-/OUT-) so a ticket's `traces_to` can point at one and the scope gate can check it. board/plan.md is a generated mirror of this file and is never the source of truth.

planVersion.description: Schema generation of this file. Still 1: the initiatives layer is purely additive — a plan written before it stays valid and is never rewritten merely because it was read — so there is nothing for a migrating release to migrate.

sections.description: One key per plan section. A section absent, empty, or holding only placeholder text counts as unfilled toward the completeness percentage.

initiatives.description: Independently valuable outcomes, each owning several epics. OPTIONAL and absent from most plans — a project with no initiative behaves exactly as it did before this section existed. Never required here: legacy plans must stay valid.

goal.description: What success means for the whole project — not a feature list.

text.description: One or two sentences: the outcome the project exists to produce.

metrics.description: Measurable signals that the goal was met.

scope.description: The boundary the scope gate enforces. `out` entries carry ids so a ticket can be caught tracing to work the plan deliberately excluded.

in.description: Free-text statements of what is in scope. Narrative only — the enforceable in-scope surface is the ids in deliverables/useCases/functional/nonFunctional/milestones.

text.description: Something this project deliberately will not do. A ticket tracing to this id is a scope violation.

item.description: A plain id'd item with no initiative ownership. Used by `openQuestions`, which stays project-level: a question owed by a human is not owned by a slice of the plan. Deliverables use `ownedItem` instead — the two were one definition until initiatives landed, and merging them again would silently make ownership legal on open questions.

ownedItem.description: An id'd item that an initiative may own. Ownership is legal on exactly six sections — deliverables, useCases, functional, nonFunctional, milestones, risks — and validatePlan()'s OWNED_SECTIONS is the check that actually runs. The two must agree.

initiativeId.description: The initiative that owns this item. Omit it for a project-wide item that applies to every initiative. An epic or ticket may trace only to a project-wide item or to one owned by its own initiative.

initiative.description: A scoped mini-plan: an independently valuable outcome delivered by several epics. It OWNS deliverables and requirements rather than nesting copies of them, so plan ids stay globally unique and every existing `traces_to` keeps working. Initiatives are never traceable themselves — a ticket traces to the requirement it implements and derives its initiative through its epic.

name.description: Short name. Never a technical layer — "Customer onboarding", not "Backend".

outcome.description: What is true for someone once this lands. An initiative without one is a folder, which is the thing this layer is not.

scope.description: This initiative's boundary. Narrative only — unlike the project's scope, these carry no ids and the scope gate does not read them. The enforceable boundary is the project's.

metrics.description: Measurable signals that this initiative's outcome was reached.

depends_on.description: Other initiatives this one assumes. PLANNING METADATA ONLY: validated for existence and cycles, and deliberately never read by ticket eligibility or lane assignment. Scheduling stays the board's job — same-epic, same-area, depends_on, and touches.

actor.description: Who performs it. Blank is allowed but weakens the use case.

text.description: What the actor does, and why it matters to them.

initiativeId.description: The initiative that owns this item. Omit it for a project-wide item that applies to every initiative. An epic or ticket may trace only to a project-wide item or to one owned by its own initiative.

text.description: One behaviour the system must have. One requirement per entry — an entry with 'and' in it is usually two.

verify.description: How it is demonstrated: a test command, a manual check, a metric. The release gate reads this.

initiativeId.description: The initiative that owns this item. Omit it for a project-wide item that applies to every initiative. An epic or ticket may trace only to a project-wide item or to one owned by its own initiative.

enforce.description: A command that MUST exit 0. The difference between a rule agents are asked to honour and one they cannot violate: `verify` is read and judged, `enforce` is executed. `maestro plan check` runs every one of these (wire it into CI); the release gate runs those a ticket traces to, and a non-zero exit is a hard no-go, never a judgment call.

text.description: The quality attribute: performance, security, availability, accessibility, compliance, operability.

budget.description: The measurable bar — 'p95 < 300ms', 'WCAG 2.2 AA', '99.9% monthly'. An NFR with no budget cannot be gated.

initiativeId.description: The initiative that owns this item. Omit it for a project-wide item that applies to every initiative. An epic or ticket may trace only to a project-wide item or to one owned by its own initiative.

verify.description: How the budget is measured. The release gate requires evidence against this for any ticket tracing here.

enforce.description: A command that MUST exit 0, encoding this quality bar as a check rather than an instruction — a forbidden-pattern grep, a lint rule, a budget assertion, a privacy invariant. Run by `maestro plan check` and by the release gate for any ticket tracing here.

target.description: Optional date or condition. Free text — the kit never schedules from it.

initiativeId.description: The initiative that owns this item. Omit it for a project-wide item that applies to every initiative. An epic or ticket may trace only to a project-wide item or to one owned by its own initiative.
The initiative that owns this item. Omit it for a project-wide item that applies to every initiative. An epic or ticket may trace only to a project-wide item or to one owned by its own initiative.

gap.description: Something a reporting skill (atomic-report, repo-audit, scale, data-model, orchestration-health) found the plan does not cover. Open REQUIRED gaps count against the completeness percentage; optional ones are suggestions and never do.

text.description: The gap, stated as what the plan is missing — not as a fix.

need.description: required = the plan is incomplete without it; optional = worth considering.

from.description: The skill or person that raised it, e.g. "atomic-report".

status.description: open = unaddressed; accepted = folded into the plan (record the id it became in `resolvedAs`); declined = deliberately not doing it. Only `open` affects completeness.

resolvedAs.description: The plan item id this gap became when accepted, e.g. "FR-7".
